deed: Gertrude Elion develops some of the first successful leukemia drugs and drugs against transplant rejection
title: Gertrude Elion developed one of the first successful drugs for childhood leukemia and a drug that made organ transplants possible

trailer.text: Gertrude Elion was a chemist and drug developer who worked for 39 years at Burroughs Wellcome and headed the Department of Experimental Therapy there.
Gertrude Elion, who was born in New York in 1918 to Jewish immigrant parents, won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1988.
She wrote that her grandfather, whom she loved dearly, died of cancer when she was 15, and that this motivated her to do something that might lead to a cure for the disease.
In 1944 Hitchings hired her to work in the laboratory at Burroughs Wellcome.
According to the National Academy of Sciences, she developed two of the first successful drugs for leukemia, as well as azathioprine, which prevents the rejection of kidney transplants.
According to PBS, in combination with other drugs, doctors eventually reached a cure rate of about 80 percent with her drug, 6-MP.

paragraphs.text: According to Elion, her father emigrated from Lithuania to the United States at the age of 12, and her mother came at the age of 14.
According to the Archive, her father came from a long line of rabbis.
When she was 15, her grandfather, whom she loved dearly, died of cancer.
She wrote that this death motivated her to do something that might lead to a cure for the disease.
According to Elion, her father had invested heavily in the stock market and went bankrupt in the crash of 1929.
She wrote that had Hunter College not been a free college, she might never have received a higher education.

stations.title: A chemist no one wanted to hire

paragraphs.text: Elion said that nobody took her seriously, and that people wondered why she wanted to be a chemist when no women were doing that.
According to Blood Cancer UK, looking for a job in the male-dominated field of chemistry was tough.
According to Encyclopedia.com, 15 graduate schools rejected her when she applied for a laboratory assistantship.
She worked as a laboratory assistant for a chemist who could not pay her a salary, because she thought the experience would be worthwhile.
After a year and a half in that job, she was earning $20 a week.
She said that she was the only woman in her graduate chemistry class, and that no one minded.
She then did analytical quality control work for a major food company, work she found repetitive.
According to the National Academy of Sciences, she measured the acidity of pickles and the color of mayonnaise there.
She wrote that it took seven years of various jobs before a shortage of men gave her the opportunity to prove herself.
According to the National Women's History Museum in the United States, Elion received a Master of Science degree in 1941.
According to PBS, Elion heard about Burroughs Wellcome through her father, and in 1944 Hitchings hired her there for $50 a week.
According to the National Women's History Museum, this was two years after Hitchings himself began working at Burroughs Wellcome, in 1942.
She said that Hitchings allowed her to learn quickly and to take on more and more responsibility when she was ready.
She described the early work as exploring new frontiers, at a time when very little was known about nucleic acid biosynthesis and the enzymes involved with it.
According to the National Women's History Museum, in the 1950s Elion and Hitchings developed a systematic method for rational drug design, as opposed to trial-and-error approaches.

According to Encyclopedia.com, in 1967 and for many years after, Elion was probably the only woman in a senior position at a major pharmaceutical company, and she reportedly felt that she experienced no discrimination at Burroughs Wellcome.
According to the Jewish Women's Archive, purine compounds and their derivatives were used to inhibit the growth of pathogenic cells by blocking the synthesis of certain nucleic acids.
According to the National Academy of Sciences, by 1949 Elion had synthesized a purine that inhibited the growth of leukemia in mice.
Burchenal used it to treat four patients, and two of them went into remission.
According to Encyclopedia.com, in the initial trials the drug was toxic, and after refinements it performed effectively and safely.
According to the National Academy of Sciences, to make 6MP Elion replaced an oxygen atom on the purine ring with a sulfur atom.
6-mercaptopurine was the first purine antagonist to be useful in the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in children.
The FDA approved it late in 1953, only ten months after clinical trials began.

According to the National Women's History Museum, Elion spent six years researching the most effective combination of 6-MP with other drugs against childhood leukemia, and today this approach cures most patients.
According to PBS, in combination with other drugs, doctors reached a cure rate of about 80 percent.

According to Blood Cancer UK, mercaptopurine is used today to treat acute lymphoblastic leukemia and acute promyelocytic leukemia, and is responsible for the increase in survival rates in childhood blood cancer.

According to Harvard SITN, the drug also temporarily affects normally dividing cells, such as cells of the immune system, hair follicles and the digestive system, and this explains side effects of chemotherapy.
According to the Jewish Women's Archive, Elion helped develop the immunosuppressant drug that made organ transplants possible.
According to PBS, by 1961 kidney transplants on humans were attempted, and with the help of Imuran patients began to survive.
According to the National Women's History Museum, Elion and Hitchings showed that drugs targeting bacterial and viral DNA could fight infectious diseases.
From this came the drugs pyrimethamine and trimethoprim.
Elion wrote that in 1967 she was appointed Head of the Department of Experimental Therapy, and that she remained in the position until she retired in 1983.
According to PBS, her team developed acyclovir, which is effective against herpes, shingles and Epstein-Barr virus.
According to the National Women's History Museum, another scientist first synthesized acyclovir, and Elion was the one who determined exactly how it works.
According to PBS, within a year of her retirement her unit used her methods to develop AZT, the first drug licensed in the United States to treat HIV.
According to Encyclopedia.com, most of the drugs she invented are included in the World Health Organization's list of essential drugs.
Elion wrote that the satisfaction of seeing people get well from diseases such as leukemia, kidney failure and herpes encephalitis cannot be described in words.
The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1988 was awarded jointly to Black, Elion and Hitchings, for their discoveries of important principles for drug treatment.
According to PBS, the Nobel Committee noted that the laureates introduced a more rational approach to drug development, as opposed to the chemical modification of natural products.
According to Encyclopedia.com, the Nobel Committee rarely honors drug developers.
On 8 December 1988, Elion delivered her Nobel Lecture at Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm.
According to the Jewish Women's Archive, in 1991 Elion was the first woman inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
She also received the Cain Award of the American Association for Cancer Research,
honorary degrees
and many patents.
According to Encyclopedia.com, such a number of patents was rare for a woman.
According to the Jewish Women's Archive, as head of the laboratory Elion made sure that her staff received credit for their work, and did not take it for herself.
She said that what they were aiming at was getting people well, and that this satisfaction is much greater than any prize.
According to the Jewish Women's Archive, Elion lost her fiancé and never married.
According to Massive Science, she doubted that she would have been so successful if she had had children.
According to the National Academy of Sciences, Elion collapsed on her daily walk and was taken to the University of North Carolina Hospital in Chapel Hill.
She died there at the age of 81.

unknowns.text: According to the National Academy of Sciences, by 1949 Elion had synthesized a purine that inhibited growth in mouse leukemia, and Joseph Burchenal of the Sloan Kettering Institute used it to treat four patients with chronic granulocytic leukemia, two of whom went into remission.

According to the Jewish Women's Archive, Elion helped develop the immunosuppressant drug that made organ transplants possible, and the archive identifies the drug for kidney transplants as azathioprine. According to PBS, azathioprine is Imuran: by 1961 kidney transplants were attempted on humans, and with the help of Imuran patients began to survive, so the sources link the two.

claims.quote: Gertrude B. Elion held her Nobel Lecture on 8 December 1988, at Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm.

claims.quote: the American Association of Cancer Research Cain Award (1985)

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה הלאומית למדעים, אליון קיבלה את פרס קיין של האגודה האמריקנית לחקר הסרטן ב-1984.
claims.quote: the Cain Award from the American Association for Cancer Research in 1984

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הנשים היהודיות, אליון קיבלה לצד פרס נובל עשרים תארי כבוד.
claims.quote: In addition to the 1988 Nobel Prize and twenty honorary doctoral degrees, Elion received the Garvan Medal

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה הלאומית למדעים, אליון החזיקה ב-45 פטנטים וב-23 תארי כבוד.
claims.quote: as well as holder of 45 patents, 23 honorary degrees, and a long list of other honors

claims.text: לפי הרווארד SITN, אליון קיבלה 26 תארי כבוד.
claims.quote: Dr. Elion received 26 honorary doctorate degrees, the National Medal of Science, admission into the Royal Society, and the Nobel Prize in Medicine.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה דוט קום, אליון החזיקה ביותר מ-40 פטנטים, נדירות בקרב נשים.
claims.quote: Gertrude Elion held over 40 patents, a rarity for a woman.

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הנשים היהודיות, אליון דאגה שעובדיה יקבלו קרדיט על עבודתם במקום לקחת אותו לעצמה כראש המעבדה.
claims.quote: ensuring they received credit for their work instead of taking the credit she would normally be given as head of the lab where the work was done

claims.text: אליון אמרה שמה שכיוונו אליו היה להבריא אנשים, וסיפוק זה גדול בהרבה מכל פרס.
claims.quote: What we were aiming at was getting people well, and the satisfaction of that is much greater than any prize you can get.

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הנשים היהודיות, אליון איבדה אתארוסה ולא נישאה מעולם.
claims.quote: During this period, she also suffered the death of her fiancé and never married.

claims.text: לפי Massive Science, אליון הטילה ספק שהייתה מצליחה כל כך אילו היו לה ילדים.
claims.quote: Elion expressed doubt that she would have been so successful if she had children

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה הלאומית למדעים, אליון התמוטטה בהליכתה היומית, נלקחה לבית החולים באוניברסיטת צפון קרוליינה בצ'אפל היל ומתה בגיל 81.
claims.quote: Trudy collapsed and was taken to the University of North Carolina Hospital in Chapel Hill, where she died at midnight at age eighty-one.

claims.text: לפי אליון, היא קיבלה תואר שני במדעים בכימיה ב-1941.
claims.quote: obtained my Master of Science degree in chemistry in 1941

claims.text: אליון כתבה שבחרה להישאר בעבודתה ולוותר על הדוקטורט.
claims.quote: I made what was then a critical decision in my life, to stay with my job and give up the pursuit of a doctorate.

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הנשים היהודיות, אליון נאלצה לעזוב את התוכנית לדוקטורט כשדיקן המכללה הציב בפניה בחירה בין לימודיה לעבודתה.
claims.quote: She began the doctoral program at Brooklyn Polytechnic but was forced to leave after two years when the college dean made her choose between her education and her job.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה דוט קום, אליון קיבלה אישור FDA ל-6MP ב-1953, וב-1975 סינתזה עם היצ'ינגס את אקיקלוביר, הטיפול היעיל הראשון בהרפס.
claims.quote: In 1975, Elion and Hitchings synthesized the drug acyclovir, the first effective treatment for herpes.

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הנשים היהודיות, אליון מתה ביום ראשון, 21 בפברואר 1999, בצ'אפל היל שבצפון קרוליינה.
claims.quote: Gertrude Elion died on Sunday, February 21, 1999, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, where she lived.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה דוט קום, אליון מתה ב-20 בפברואר 1999 בצ'אפל היל.
claims.quote: She died on February 20, 1999, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

claims.text: לפי המוזיאון הלאומי להיסטוריה של נשים בארצות הברית, אליון קיבלה תואר שני במדעים ב-1941.
claims.quote: finally earning her Master of Science in 1941

claims.text: לפי האקדמיה הלאומית למדעים, היא פיתחה שתיים מהתרופות המוצלחות הראשונות ללוקמיה, וגם את אזתיופרין, שמונע דחייה של השתלות כליה.
claims.quote: an agent to prevent the rejection of kidney transplants
